title: How Long Does an Iron Infusion Take? Everything Brisbane Patients Need to Know
html:
How Long Does an Iron Infusion Take?

This is one of the most common questions we receive from patients considering iron infusion therapy – and it is a practical one. You need to know how to plan your day.

The straightforward answer is: the infusion itself takes between 15 and 60 minutes, depending on the iron product used and the dose prescribed. However, your total appointment time – including the pre-infusion consultation and the post-infusion observation period – will typically be 60 to 90 minutes.

Here is a detailed breakdown of what to expect.

Before the Infusion: The Consultation (15–20 Minutes)

Every iron infusion at Australian Longevity Clinic begins with a brief consultation with our doctor or nurse. During this time, we will:

  • Review your blood test results confirming iron deficiency
  • Check your medical history and current medications for any contraindications
  • Confirm the appropriate iron product and dose for your situation
  • Answer any questions you have about the procedure

If you are a new patient and have not yet had a blood test, we will arrange this before scheduling your infusion. Iron infusions cannot be administered without confirmed blood test results showing iron deficiency.

The Infusion Itself: 15 to 60 Minutes

Once the consultation is complete, a small cannula is inserted into a vein in your arm – this takes less than a minute. The iron solution is then connected and delivered at a controlled rate.

The duration of the infusion depends on the specific iron product being used:

| Iron Product | Typical Infusion Time | |---|---| | Ferric carboxymaltose (Ferinject) | 15–30 minutes | | Iron polymaltose (Ferrum H) | 30–60 minutes | | Low molecular weight iron dextran | 60 minutes |

Ferric carboxymaltose (Ferinject) is one of the products used at Australian Longevity Clinic. It can deliver a full therapeutic dose in a short infusion time, making it a practical option for many patients.

During the infusion, you can relax, use your phone, read, or work on a laptop. Most patients find the experience comfortable and unremarkable. Some patients notice a slight metallic taste during the infusion – this is normal and resolves quickly.

After the Infusion: Observation Period (15–30 Minutes)

After the infusion is complete, we ask all patients to remain at the clinic for a minimum of 15 minutes. This is a standard precaution to monitor for any delayed reactions, which – while rare – can occasionally occur with IV iron.

During this time, our clinical staff will check in with you and remove the cannula once you are ready to leave. Most patients feel completely well during this period and leave without any issues.

Can I Drive Myself Home?

Yes. Unlike some medical procedures, iron infusions do not require sedation or anaesthesia, and you can drive yourself to and from the appointment. You can also return to work or normal activities immediately after leaving the clinic.

What Should I Do Before My Iron Infusion?

Eating and drinking: You do not need to fast before an iron infusion. In fact, eating a normal meal beforehand is recommended, as some patients feel slightly lightheaded if they arrive hungry.

Clothing: Wear comfortable clothing with sleeves that can be easily rolled up to allow access to the vein in your arm.

Medications: Continue taking your regular medications as normal unless specifically advised otherwise by our doctor.

Blood tests: Bring your most recent blood test results if you have them. If you do not have recent results, we can arrange a blood test before your infusion appointment.

How Soon Will I Feel Better?

The timeline for iron stores to normalise following an infusion varies between individuals and depends on the severity of deficiency and other clinical factors. A follow-up blood test is recommended 6 to 8 weeks after the infusion to confirm that iron levels have been adequately restored.
